claim_sentences: Read it as INTENT, not as a guarantee the call will succeed: it names a side from the class table and never checks that side is registered, so form_function_rotate resolves to A while only its Path B exists, and the default dispatch raises DispatchError.
path must be 'A' or 'B' — 'verify' is a dispatcher mode, never a registered side, and raises ValueError here.
'verify' is a dispatcher mode rather than a registered side and raises ValueError.

This is the non-raising probe -- reach for it instead of wrapping lookup in a try/except UnknownOperationError, which is the same question asked expensively, and instead of testing membership in registered_ops(), which tells you the op exists but not which sides it has.
``leaf_dim`` below 52 is a ValueError, not a silent split: the header must fit one leaf.
Complex input is refused with TypeError, matching NumPy;
an n-D input or a non-default axis raises ValueError on the numpy-free path.
Both an unterminated ``{...`` and an unknown key raise ``ValueError`` — there is no silent partial render.
``format`` will happily evaluate attribute and index syntax inside the braces (a real injection surface for descriptor-supplied templates) and raises on stray braces in the literal text;
Domain: x <= 0 raises ValueError (log 0 = -Inf is not a rational);
Writing 1j/(k2 - m*m) yourself produces a ZeroDivisionError or an inf at the pole;
It owns the ENGINE-VERSION contract: if any chain is present, ``[catalog].chain_schema_version`` must exist and equal ``ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION`` (1), else ``ChainSpecError``.
